answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to post a refundable stake before it may bridge value across services, so creating thousands of fake identities becomes expensive rather than free. Reputation then accrues slowly through verified work: a newcomer that behaves like the raven in the old fable — taking the grain and flying off — loses its stake and its history, while honest agents compound trust over time. Attackers face a real cost per identity, and the stake makes mass forgery unprofitable.
